evidence.text: Image-checksum mismatches appeared only after the vectorized decoder feature was enabled for part of the fleet.
All initially affected hosts used ARM64 processors, but most ARM64 hosts did not show corruption.
No checksum mismatches occurred on x86_64 hosts with the vectorized decoder enabled.
No checksum mismatches occurred on ARM64 hosts where the vectorized decoder remained disabled.
Affected ARM64 hosts also used the new pooled-buffer allocator; some unaffected ARM64 hosts used the same allocator with vectorization disabled.

On ARM64 workers using the pooled-buffer allocator at concurrency 32, enabling vectorization reproduced 7 checksum mismatches in 500,000 decodes. The test did not vary architecture and allocator in the same run.
On ARM64 workers at concurrency 32 using the legacy allocator, vectorization produced no mismatches in 500,000 decodes.
On x86_64 workers using vectorization and the pooled-buffer allocator, no mismatch appeared in 100,000 decodes, but those workers ran at concurrency 16 because the test harness could not sustain 32.
Reducing concurrency to 8 on affected ARM64 hosts stopped corruption without changing architecture, vectorization, or allocator.
The corruption occurs after a buffer is returned to the pool while a vectorized decode still references a slice from that buffer.
Storage-object checksums match at read time, before decode begins.
One affected availability zone had elevated storage latency, but affected hosts also existed in a zone without the latency increase.
Huge-page settings were not captured consistently across affected and unaffected hosts during the incident.

A matched decoder test held vectorization enabled, pooled-buffer allocator enabled, and concurrency at 32 workers while varying only architecture. ARM64 recorded 8 checksum mismatches in 600,000 decodes; x86_64 recorded 0 in 600,000.
One affected rack ran a newer NIC firmware revision, but checksum mismatches also occurred on affected hosts with the older revision and did not occur on x86_64 hosts using either revision.
Buffer-pool size differed in one availability zone, but corruption occurred in both default-size and enlarged-pool zones when the failing decoder combination was present.
Affected source images had a broad range of compression ratios, and mismatch frequency did not cluster around any compression-ratio band in the retained sample.

hypotheses.text: ARM64 architecture materially increases corruption risk even without the pooled-buffer and vectorization combination.
The vectorized decoder materially increases corruption risk even when the pooled-buffer allocator is not active.
The observed corruption depends on the joint presence of ARM64, vectorization, pooled-buffer reuse, and sufficiently high concurrency.
Corrupted storage objects were the initiating source of the checksum mismatches.

actions.text: Disable vectorization on ARM64 pooled-buffer hosts while a safe ownership fix is implemented.
Evacuate the affected availability zone as the primary corrective action.
Allow decoder outputs to proceed without checksum validation during the incident.
Reduce decoder concurrency on affected hosts from current levels to 8 workers.
Replace source storage objects for affected jobs.
